content: Building on some recent discussion related to this, I'd like to ask the community what we think the statement of the Jordan Curve Theorem will be once it is formalized into mathlib. I'm not sure whether anyone is actually actively working on formalizing the JCT itself, but I think having an agreed-upon statement even without a proof would unlock a lot. For example, I am working on defining the interiors of polygons, but to do this right requires the JCT. So what will the JCT look like? Will the ambient space be only EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), any manifold homeomorphic to that, or something else? How is the statement itself likely to look?

This is a great question. Smooth Jordan curves show up twice in recent Annals papers, once defined as maps into R2\R^2R2 and once defined as maps into C\mathbb{C}C. I asked about putting the definition into mathlib a few weeks ago and was told that probably mathlib didn't want a definition.
cc @Sébastien Gouëzel
I feel like there's enough discussion for an issue to collect all of it: #35222

Here is a version of the Jordan curve theorem as I envision it in Mathlib: let E be a finite dimensional normed real vector space of dimension \ge 2, let f : sphere (0 : E) 1 -> E be a continuous injective map, then E \ range f has two connected components.
With specialized versions when the dimension is 2, and the source of f could be any of our versions of the circle

The statement in #mathlib4 > Jordan curve / Smooth Jordan curve @ 💬 is already pretty close to the established statement in HOL Light (see p.7 in the linked PDF in forwarded message below); I think it's good to generalize it to 2D real normed space. I've also wondered whether we should define winding numbers in 2D real normed space; probably I'll just define it first for Complex then transport by homeomorphisms.

Junyan Xu said:

This is another nice account of the development of simplicial homology in HOL light: it also covers the Jordan-Schoenflies theorem (a strengthening of Jordan curve theorem that requires complex analysis) and the Jordan-Brouwer separation theorem (higher dimensional generalization).
Out of curiosity, is anyone currently working on JCT?
I have a full proof of the Jordan Curve Theorem (2D version), reformalized (using LLMs) from Hales' HOL Light proof . Is it of interest for mathlib or anyone?

I am interested (unless it's AI). (Edit: the above message was edited to clarify that this is indeed AI)
As for Mathlib, likely not.
It is AI, sorry ^^
You could dump it in merely-true, a repository for AI-driven Lean formalization.
sounds good ^^
IANAL but that seems to be in violation of the license of the HOL Light proof, since the merely-true repo requires "Contributors agree to license their contributions under the Apache 2.0 License."
Good point, thanks. I'll double-check that :)

That license objection would also be true for mathlib. I would also recommend merely-true. All that will happen if you try to PR it to mathlib is that people will complain that the code is not of an extremely high quality and you'll find it hard to get reviewers. The whole point of merely-true is that you don't have to go through the review process.
I believe the quality is irrelevant here since such a project regardless of quality doesn't fit Mathlib's generalization requirements (I think).

Also for licensing, that probably depends on the line between "modification" and "rewrite".
You said it is "reformalized", and I'm not sure on what side that falls on.

Oh I mostly expected that it would not be good enough code quality for mathlib, and also that mathlib may want a more general version (which though? I would maybe like to tackle the generalization). It was a fun experiment.

(Yes, I don't know if a rewrite in a different language technically counts as a modification)

OTOH if you mean help Mathlib get closer to JCT by contributing small PRs towards it, even if they're LLM generated, then that sounds great to me. But again should probably be coordinated with others to not step on their progress.

Sure!

def IsSimpleClosedCurve (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℝ → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
    C = f '' Icc 0 1 ∧
    Continuous f ∧
    Set.InjOn f (Ico 0 1) ∧
    f 0 = f 1

It is a direct translation from HOL Light's proof, so I suppose it's not the most mathlib-correct way to state it.

Is this equivelent to, and preferably replaced by

def IsSimpleClosedCurve (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : Prop := Nonempty (C ≃ₜ UnitAddCircle)

?

Sure, here it is:

Proof that ∀ C, IsSimpleClosedCurve2 C = IsSimpleClosedCurve C

example : ∀ C, IsSimpleClosedCurve2 C = IsSimpleClosedCurve C := by
  intro C; apply propext; constructor
  · -- ⇒: Nonempty (C ≃ₜ UnitAddCircle) → IsSimpleClosedCurve C
    rintro ⟨e⟩
    refine ⟨fun t => ↑(e.symm (↑t : UnitAddCircle)), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · -- C = f '' Icc 0 1
      ext c; simp only [mem_image]; constructor
      · intro hc
        set q := e ⟨c, hc⟩; have ht := (equivIco 1 0 q).2
        refine ⟨(equivIco 1 0 q).1, Ico_subset_Icc_self (by simpa using ht), ?_⟩
        change (e.symm (↑(equivIco 1 0 q).1 : UnitAddCircle) : E2') = c
        rw [(equivIco 1 0).injective ((equivIco_coe_eq ht).trans rfl)]
        exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.symm_apply_apply ⟨c, hc⟩)
      · rintro ⟨t, _, rfl⟩; exact (e.symm (↑t : UnitAddCircle)).2
    · exact continuous_subtype_val.comp (e.symm.continuous.comp (AddCircle.continuous_mk' 1))
    · -- InjOn f (Ico 0 1)
      intro a ha b hb hab
      exact (coe_eq_coe_iff_of_mem_Ico ⟨ha.1, by linarith [ha.2]⟩ ⟨hb.1, by linarith [hb.2]⟩).mp
        (e.symm.injective (Subtype.val_injective hab))
    · -- f 0 = f 1
      change (e.symm (↑(0 : ℝ) : UnitAddCircle) : E2') =
        (e.symm (↑(1 : ℝ) : UnitAddCircle) : E2')
      exact congrArg (fun x => (e.symm x : E2')) (by simp [coe_period])
  · -- ⇐: IsSimpleClosedCurve C → Nonempty (C ≃ₜ UnitAddCircle)
    rintro ⟨f, hCf, hcont, hinj, hf01⟩
    have hg_cont := liftIco_zero_continuous hf01 hcont.continuousOn
    have hg_inj : Injective (liftIco 1 0 f) := by
      intro x y hxy
      have hx := (equivIco 1 0 x).2; have hy := (equivIco 1 0 y).2
      simp only [zero_add, mem_Ico] at hx hy
      exact (equivIco 1 0).injective (Subtype.val_injective (hinj hx hy hxy))
    have hg_range : range (liftIco 1 0 f) = C := by
      rw [hCf]; ext c; constructor
      · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
        have hx := (equivIco 1 0 x).2; simp only [zero_add, mem_Ico] at hx
        exact ⟨_, Ico_subset_Icc_self hx, rfl⟩
      · rintro ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
        by_cases ht1 : t = 1
        · exact ⟨↑(0 : ℝ), by
            rw [liftIco_coe_apply (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ∈ Ico 0 (0+1)), ht1, hf01]⟩
        · exact ⟨↑t, liftIco_coe_apply ⟨ht.1, by linarith [lt_of_le_of_ne ht.2 ht1]⟩⟩
    have hmem : ∀ x, liftIco 1 0 f x ∈ C := fun x => hg_range ▸ mem_range_self x
    let g' : UnitAddCircle → C := fun x => ⟨_, hmem x⟩
    have hg'_cont : Continuous g' := continuous_induced_rng.mpr hg_cont
    exact ⟨(Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2
      (f := .ofBijective g' ⟨fun x y h => hg_inj (congrArg Subtype.val h),
        fun ⟨c, hc⟩ => (hg_range ▸ hc).elim fun x hx => ⟨x, Subtype.val_injective hx⟩⟩)
      hg'_cont).symm⟩
